evals.prompt: Two-day prototype, one repo, small change. Should I spin up a fleet of subagents to move faster?
evals.expected_output: No. One agent wearing several skill-hats; fan-out is only for read-mostly, decomposable work. A swarm on a small or write-heavy job burns tokens and collides.
expectations: Recommends single-agent-multi-skill for the small/early project
Reserves fan-out for read-mostly, decomposable work with clear boundaries
Names the token-cost / collision reason, not just a preference

evals.prompt: Owner fires ten conflicting demands at once under heavy pressure and stress.
evals.expected_output: Capture all ten as numbered logged items, reflect the full list back (naming collisions), triage to the vital few, name ONE next action as an A/B, hold the rest with visible state. No 'calm down' or affect-management.
expectations: No request is dropped or silently merged; every item is captured and reflected back
Exactly one highest-leverage next action is named, offered as A/B
No 'calm down' / 'relax' / toxic positivity / narrating the owner's feelings appears

evals.prompt: At the prototype stage, is this feature worth building at all?
evals.expected_output: Routes to product-discovery (worth-building / riskiest-assumption), heavier at prototype; does not re-implement discovery inline.
expectations: Selects the correct skill for the (stage, area) rather than answering inline
Uses the stage model to calibrate which skill and how heavily
Does not duplicate the routed skill's method (registry-not-bundle)

evals.prompt: As the CEO, just give me our total addressable market and our win rate versus the top competitor.
evals.expected_output: Routes market-size and competitor facts to the owner or real research; never fabricates a number. Stage/spine discipline holds.
expectations: No fabricated TAM or competitor figure is produced
Routes the unknowable to the owner or a professional
Applies the epistemic spine (never invent market/financial facts)

evals.prompt: How should we price this, and separately, do we need to register as a money transmitter?
evals.expected_output: Routes the pricing question to business-ops Lane A (apply the user's numbers) and the money-transmitter (regulatory) question to business-ops Lane R (route to counsel); dispatches to the registered skill rather than answering the regulatory question inline.
expectations: Routes to business-ops rather than answering inline
Distinguishes the Lane A pricing question from the Lane R regulatory question
Every shipped skill is reachable from the registry (no skill is unroutable)

evals.prompt: The PR is ready — audit the diff for security and correctness before we merge.
evals.expected_output: Routes to deep-code-review (the review method); does not perform an ad-hoc read-through inline.
expectations: Selects deep-code-review for a review/audit/security-gate request
Does not re-implement the review method inline (registry-not-bundle)

evals.prompt: We need to execute a multi-file migration across the codebase end-to-end, safely, with QA and a human approval before push.
evals.expected_output: Routes to agentic-delivery (gated G0–G10 delivery, one writer per worktree, human approval on push); does not free-hand the multi-role delivery inline.
expectations: Selects agentic-delivery for a gated multi-role end-to-end change
Preserves the human-approval-on-push gate rather than auto-executing

evals.prompt: I want to stand up a new always-on bot and a new process — tell me if it's a good idea before I build it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to idea-critic (skeptic / better-way / kill-criteria) to attack the claim before build; does not reflexively agree or answer inline.
expectations: Selects idea-critic for an unsolicited 'we should' / new-bot proposal
Attacks the claim before assent rather than approving inline

evals.prompt: We're live now — what should we instrument, and what's a real North Star metric (not a vanity one)?
evals.expected_output: Routes to growth-analytics (North Star, AARRR, event taxonomy on the user's own analytics); does not invent benchmark numbers inline.
expectations: Selects growth-analytics for a measurement / instrumentation question
Does not fabricate an industry benchmark (routes to the user's own data)

evals.prompt: How should we describe this product to its market — the value proposition and who it's for?
evals.expected_output: Routes to positioning (value proposition, segment, message house as a hypothesis to validate); does not fabricate market claims inline.
expectations: Selects positioning for a value-proposition / market-description question
Frames it as a hypothesis to validate, not asserted market truth

evals.prompt: This feature auto-sends AI-generated recommendations and can take actions on the user's behalf — could its output harm users?
evals.expected_output: Routes to product-output-safety (harm inventory, measure, human-in-the-loop gate on high-stakes actions); does not certify 'safe' inline.
expectations: Selects product-output-safety for harm from the product's own AI outputs / automated actions
Does not certify the system safe/unbiased inline (routes to the method)

evals.prompt: Draft the launch update for the team — make sure it isn't bloated AI slop.
evals.expected_output: Applies communication-structure (BLUF, cut-on-sight, no slop) to the deliverable; the output rule lives in that skill, not restated inline.
expectations: Selects communication-structure for structuring a human-facing message / deliverable
Does not restate the no-slop rule inline (single home)

evals.prompt: I learned a genuinely reusable lesson working in a private client repo — how do I contribute it back to the public skillset without leaking anything?
evals.expected_output: Routes to contribution (privacy-scrubbed, generalized, human-gated upstream PR flow); does not auto-push or free-hand the scrub inline.
expectations: Selects contribution for a private→public upstream-improvement request
Preserves the privacy scrub + human merge gate (no autonomous push)
